name: Fern Canyon
where: Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park, Redwood National and State Parks, Orick, California
blurb: A 50-foot canyon hung with ferns behind Gold Bluffs Beach, a coast-and-ridge loop with Roosevelt elk, and the James Irvine Trail through old-growth redwoods.

trails.name: James Irvine Trail to Fern Canyon

status: Open (Nov 19, 2026). Fern Canyon and Davison Road open (two stream crossings, high clearance recommended); seasonal footbridges are out, so expect ankle- to knee-deep water. Easternmost stairs between Fern Canyon and the James Irvine Trail closed for construction; Miner’s Ridge Trail blocked by a downed tree; Newton B. Drury Parkway closed since Nov 17 for high winds (visitor center via Hwy 101 exit 753). Free parking reservation required May 15–Sep 15 to drive to Fern Canyon.

rare.why: California's Roosevelt elk fell to as few as 15 animals by 1925; protected herds at Gold Bluffs Beach and Prairie Creek helped them rebound to more than 1,000, and hikers come to Fern Canyon to see them.
An endangered seabird that nests in the old-growth redwoods of the park.
A federally threatened shorebird seen along Gold Bluffs Beach.
